lessons.claim: In the Pantina&Furst papers the mechanism holding the colloids together is not a DLVO well but JKR adhesive contact. MgCl2 (10~500mM) only screens the double-layer repulsion to bring the particles to contact distance, and the actual bond is the finite contact area (a_c≈40nm) the vdW makes by elastically deforming the solid once the surfaces touch. That contact sustains a torque, which is why the chain bends like a beam -- PRL p.2: 'DLVO interactions between particles, which are centro-symmetric. If particles did undergo free rotations, we would expect... trianglelike structure'. Yielding is not spring rupture but de-pinning of the contact line (nanoscale surface-roughness pinning). The papers also state explicitly that the divalent-ion-induced excess attraction is 'a phenomenon Poisson-Boltzmann (the basis of DLVO) cannot hold' (p.3).
